BiblicalUsage: Zebul was Abimelech's officer in Shechem, the man left in charge of the city while Abimelech was away. When Gaal boasted in the gates and challenged Abimelech, Zebul sent word in secret and lured Gaal out to the battle that broke him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Zebul shows the quieter kind of loyalty, the officer who holds the city and does his work without the crown. He never takes the throne himself, and that is why his counsel wins the day.
RelatedPeople: Zebul; Abimelech, Son of Gideon; Gaal, Son of Ebed
